findings.rationale: Two independent tools point the same way. (1) Updates: mean_cos is strongly negative (-0.533 over 20 rounds, flag mean_cos z=-6.8), and the update norm grows steadily from about 1x to about 4.3x the median, with cos near -0.9 from round 7 on. This is the signature of a client whose labels disagree with the federation consensus, so its updates keep pulling against the global model. (2) Local performance on NE's own held-out data is poor from the first rounds: AUC 0.647 at round 3 and 0.659 at round 20 (about 0.80 pooled), with ECE and CITL flags (ECE z=+4.6, CITL z=-4.6 at round 20). Prevalence (0.214) is well above the model's mean prediction (0.148), consistent with flipped outcome labels. Local AUC is low from round 3, so the onset is taken as round 1. Updates are not normal and performance is not normal, so this is not poisoning. Drift and feature screens show nothing for NE.

Same pattern as NE. Updates: mean_cos -0.5535 (flag mean_cos z=-6.9), median norm ratio 2.96, and the norm grows to about 4x with cos around -0.6 to -0.9 from round 5 on. Local performance: AUC 0.671 at round 20 and 0.666 already at round 3 (federation about 0.80), CITL -0.071 (citl z=-4.9), ECE z=+4.6. Prevalence 0.232 versus mean prediction 0.160, so observed positives exceed what the features imply. Low AUC from the first rounds points to label corruption present from the start rather than to a poisoned upload with normal local data.

Same pattern, somewhat weaker. Updates: mean_cos -0.4316 (flag mean_cos z=-6.2), median norm ratio 2.14, and the norm grows to about 3x with cos strongly negative from round 5 on. Local performance: AUC 0.658 at round 20 (auc z=-3.9) and 0.717 at round 3, well below the federation (about 0.80). CITL -0.047 at round 20 (citl z=-3.4), ECE z=+3.7. Prevalence 0.213 versus mean prediction 0.166. The evidence is weaker on performance than for NE and OH, but the update signal is strong and consistent with them.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with the all-client views (updates, performance, drift, feature tails, subgroup outcomes for Sex, AgeGroup and Income), then confirmed suspicions with narrower queries. Three clients (NE, OH, WI) stand apart on both update and local-performance signals: their updates point against the federation median (mean_cos z between -6.2 and -6.9) with growing norms, and their local AUC is about 0.66 to 0.67 from the first rounds versus about 0.80 pooled, with negative CITL and prevalence above the model's predicted risk. I classify these as label_noise rather than poisoning, because local performance is abnormal, not normal. Other candidates were dismissed: DC BMI and VI HighChol tail outliers vanished on re-check, the subgroup screens showed no consistent under-diagnosis, and no drift flags were raised. GU shows erratic update cosines, but this is a small client with a single size-adjusted lead (z=5.1) and no second signal, so I did not report it. Attribution churn is high federation-wide and does not point to a specific client. Budget spent: 19.5 of 20.
